evidence.quote: Thus, only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity in communications, reduces cost
would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events

criteria.reasoning: Mission, rationale and single-spacecraft justification are well covered with references. However, users (operator and customers) are only vaguely implied ('operated and accessed from Australia ground facilities'); no explicit operator/customer identification.

evidence.quote: an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of $ 87.7924^{\circ} $
situated very close to the equator, with a latitude of $ 45.05^{\circ} $N
An average contact duration of almost twenty minutes was achieved

criteria.reasoning: All major requirements addressed with STK evidence (screenshots, access report, ground tracks). But critical errors: SSO inclination at 600 km should be ~97.8° (retrograde), not 87.79°, contradicting their own plot; Kourou latitude stated as 45.05°N (actually ~5°N); contradictory swath/resolution discussion. Design logic otherwise sound.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions are specific and tied to report evidence, including risk acknowledgement (Vega E availability) and fallback options. Not fully detailed on all segments, so lower end of Accomplished.

Clear structure with headings and contents; figures labelled. But references are bare URLs without titles/authors, Wikipedia used (explicitly disallowed), some garbled sentences ('which is also desirable' for low resolution), and figure captions inconsistent.

technical_issues.issue: Sun-synchronous inclination at 600 km should be ~97.8° (retrograde, >90°), not 87.79°; contradicts their own inclination-vs-altitude plot and the stated 'retrograde' orbit.
Kourou's latitude stated as 45.05°N; it is ~5.2°N. The claim that two launch windows occur daily because latitude is smaller than target inclination is built on this error.
RAAN of 27.33° said to 'indicate the location of the launch facility' — RAAN is not directly set by launch site longitude without further argument.
Contradictory statement: 'A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable' — low resolution is not desirable.
Contradictory: satellite described as 'without thrusters' yet earlier an orbital manoeuvre at EOL is mentioned; drag sail choice is consistent but reasoning is muddled.

overall: Well-structured report addressing nearly all task requirements with STK evidence, but undermined by a fundamental orbital-mechanics error (SSO inclination), a factual launch-site error, weak referencing (bare URLs, Wikipedia), and vague user identification. Adequate-to-good overall; core mission design logic is otherwise reasonable.
